structure.heading: Carrier Lane and Last‑Mile Cost Driver Diagnostics with Network Change Recommendations
text_content: **Carrier Lane and Last‑Mile Cost Driver Diagnostics with Network Change Recommendations**

In the carrier lane diagnostics, the single most underperforming linehaul is Dallas, TX → Atlanta, GA at $2.18 per mile with 71% on-time performance in 2025-03. Detailed lane-level KPIs show elevated cost-per-mile driven by deadhead, low load factor, and detention; carrier scorecards indicate opportunities to renegotiate contract tiers, consolidate frequencies, and pursue dedicated capacity pilots for high-volume weekdays.

Last-mile diagnostics for 2025-04 reveal that residential delivery and fuel surcharge account for 63% of last-mile accessorials ($1.92 of $3.05 per stop) in 2025-04, concentrating margin pressure on low-density routes. Recommendations emphasize increased parcel consolidation, targeted zone skipping, and selective use of crowdshipping platforms to reduce per-stop accessorials while maintaining customer SLA compliance.

The recommended network changes — reassigning select SKUs to regional DCs, rerouting the Dallas linehaul, and implementing last-mile consolidation pilots — are projected to reduce annual transportation spend by $8.6M and improve OTIF from 92.1% to 95.0% by 2026-12-31. Implementation milestones include Q3 2025 pilot launches, contract renegotiations by 2025-10, and ongoing monthly OTIF monitoring with carrier scorecards.

structure.heading: Baseline Network Cost-to-Serve and Distribution Centre Configuration Comparison
text_content: **Baseline Network Cost-to-Serve and Distribution Centre Configuration Comparison**

pack cycle times were normalized for order mix and weight. The fiscal baseline was established using calendarized demand profiles and validated parcel audit data from January–December FY2025, providing the reference point for scenario modelling and for quantifying improvements from proposed network changes. Stakeholders have approved this baseline for modelling and signoff.

The 3-DC scenario that adds a Reno, NV distribution centre reduces the network’s average delivery distance by 14.2%, decreasing mean route mileage from 612 miles to 525 miles. Operational analysis projects shorter transit times on western lanes, improved carrier lane performance variability, and reduced long-haul trucking exposure. Benefits include lower fuel consumption, fewer multi-leg transfers, and potential reductions in damage and delay incidents. The model assumes Reno capacity sized for projected western demand, incremental staffing phased across two quarters, and contract adjustments with regional carriers to capture lane-level rate improvements and maintain existing service levels, throughput and resilience.

The recommended distribution configuration and phased carrier negotiations target savings of $1.10 per order by Q4 2026 versus the FY2025 baseline, delivering a target cost-to-serve of $11.74 per order. Execution will follow a three-phase plan beginning Q3 2025: 1) Reno DC commissioning and western route rebalancing (Q3–Q4 2025); 2) carrier lane re-bids and contractual amendments (Q1–Q2 2026); 3) last-mile optimization pilots and full rollout (Q3 2026). Key performance indicators are weekly cost-per-order, on-time delivery rate, and lane-specific yield; governance reviews are monthly through Q4 2026. Contingency budgets, carrier KPIs, and real-time dashboards will monitor progress monthly.
